pamphlet_excerpts: Point Scissors Pliers: Point scissors and pliers away from your body when workingwith reed.
Bracing Hand Away: Keep your bracing hand away from the path ofthe scissors.
Projects Complete Basketry: The projects needed to complete the Basketry merit badge weredesigned to increase your weaving skills.
Traditional Styles Ofbasket: Traditional styles ofbasket weaving are perhaps as old as the art itself, and thebasic steps are easy to learn.
step_by_step_procedure: Section Sometips Understand: This section will give you sometips to help you understand the fundamentals.
Note: The instructions and photos in this pamphletdescribe projects from a right-handed person’s viewpoint.
Left-handed Adjust Stepsso: If you are left-handed, you may adjust the stepsso that you are more comfortable.
Pocketknife Cut Willow: You can use a pocketknife to cut willow or whatever natural materials youcan gather to make a basket.

pamphlet_excerpts: Common Weaves: The following are common weaves used in this pamphlet.
Over-under Weave Plainweave: Sometimes called over-under weave, the plainweave is done with rigid stakes or spokes, and weavers thatwrap around the stakes in an over-one.
Spokes Stakes Rigid: Spokes and stakes usually are more rigid and thicker reedthan weavers.
Continuous Weave Looks: Continuous weave looks much the same as plainweave, but it is woven with a different technique.
step_by_step_procedure: Weave Created Odd: This weave is created over an odd numberof stakes.
Not Done Row: It is not done one row at a time, but continuouslyfrom beginning to end, with additional weavers added whenmore length is needed.
Method Weaving Involves: This method of weaving involves the weaverpassing over two or more stakes and under two or more stakesat a time.
Weave Pairing Involvestwo: This weave, sometimes called pairing, involvestwo weavers, each alternately twisting over and underconsecutive spokes.

pamphlet_excerpts: Beginning Weavers Start: Beginning weavers should start with a simple project andbuild on their skill by trying projects of increased difficulty.
Projects Meet: The following projects can be used to meet the merit badgerequirements, but any qualifying project will do.
Weave Squarebasket Round: To earn the Basketry merit badge, you must weave a squarebasket, a round basket, and a campstool seat.
Convenience BSA National: For your convenience, the BSA National Distribution Center hasprepackaged kits available for thesquare basket, round basket, and campstool seat.
step_by_step_procedure: Project Designed Beginner: This project, designed for the beginner who has considerablepractice in basket weaving, is both easy to make and durable.
Twill Weave Inches: It uses a twill weave. 9 by 12 inches ■ 9-by-12-inch frame ■ Several very longpieces of 1/2-inch flatreed, about 77 feet Step 1, Assemble the frame.
Soak Several Long: Step 2, Soak several long pieces of reed in water.
